positive_experience.text: Elderly patients with GI bleeding often present without hematemesis; relying solely on classic signs like hematemesis misses a significant proportion of upper GI bleeds, especially in this demographic.
Black tarry stools and coffee-ground vomiting strongly suggest upper gastrointestinal bleeding; this pattern is highly specific and should prompt immediate diagnostic workup even without hematemesis.

negative_experience.text: Fever and chills in a patient with fatigue and cough suggest systemic infection, not MDS, unless there is clear evidence of bone marrow failure or cytopenias; do not assume MDS without objective hematologic findings.

Absence of headache, visual disturbance, or bleeding in a patient with suspected dural AV fistula does not rule out the diagnosis; these are not universally present and should not be used as exclusion criteria.

Petechiae on palms and soles, combined with fever, tachycardia, dyspnea, and confusion, strongly suggest a systemic inflammatory or coagulopathy process; do not apply this pattern when the patient has no petechiae or when symptoms are isolated to a single organ system without systemic signs.
